title: A date that is always valid
description:
Write a class `Date` that can never hold nonsense such as month 13 or day 0.

- `Date(int year, int month, int day)`: a month outside 1 to 12 becomes 1; a day outside 1 to the length of that month becomes 1. February has 29 days in a leap year and 28 otherwise.
- `Date(int year)`: 1 January of that year. Write it as a **delegating constructor** that calls the three-argument one.
- `int year() const`, `int month() const`, `int day() const`.
- `static bool isLeapYear(int year)` (a `static` member function belongs to the class, not to one object; you will meet these properly in lesson 6.05, for now just put `static` in front).
hints: Fix the month first; you need a valid month before you can look up how many days it has.
